answers.(a): dy/dx = (2cos x + 1)/(2 + cos x)^2; gradient of line = 1/4, so (2cos x + 1)/(2 + cos x)^2 = 1/4 gives cos^2 x - 4cos x = 0, cos x = 0 (cos x = 4 rejected). Points: (π/2, 1/2) and (3π/2, -1/2).
answers.(b): Perpendicular gradient is -4. Setting (2cos x + 1)/(2 + cos x)^2 = -4 gives 4cos^2 x + 18cos x + 17 = 0, cos x = (-9 ± √13)/4 ≈ -1.35 or -3.15, both outside [-1, 1], so no real x. (Equivalently, since d/dc[(2c+1)/(2+c)^2] = (2-2c)/(2+c)^3 ≥ 0 on [-1,1], the gradient lies in [-1, 1/3], so it can never equal -4.)
